nodes.instructions: Name the branch after the issue (e.g. 123-short-title).

nodes.text: Brainstorm with the superpowers:brainstorming skill (if it isn't installed, do it by hand): read the issue, explore the code it touches, ask the user one question at a time until the goal is clear, propose 2-3 approaches with trade-offs, and get the user's OK on a design. Save it to docs/plans/<date>-<topic>-design.md and commit it.

Write the implementation plan with the superpowers:writing-plans skill (if it isn't installed, do it by hand): small numbered tasks, each with the exact files, the failing test to write first, the code, and the command that verifies it. Save it to docs/plans/<date>-<topic>-plan.md, commit it, and show the user the task list.

agentDone.goal: Every task in the plan is implemented and committed, and a fresh run of the project's full test suite, lint and type checks passes. Name the commands you ran and their results.

nodes.text: Take the next unfinished tasks of the plan. Implement them with superpowers:test-driven-development (failing test first, watch it fail, minimal code, watch it pass) through superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans. On any failure use superpowers:systematic-debugging: find the root cause before changing code. Never skip or delete a test. Commit each task. If one of these skills isn't installed, do the same by hand.

Use superpowers:verification-before-completion (if it isn't installed, do it by hand): run the full test suite, lint and type checks fresh and read the output. Never claim a task done without that evidence; anything failing is the next round's first job.

Ask for a code review with superpowers:requesting-code-review (if it isn't installed, launch a fresh reviewer subagent with the Agent tool yourself): a reviewer on the branch diff against the base branch; wait for its report (in the foreground). Fix every important finding, re-run the tests, and commit.

Finish the branch with superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch (if it isn't installed, do it by hand), choosing to push this branch and create a PR: a title from the issue, a description with the summary, the design and plan links, how it was tested, and "Closes #<issue>". Never push to main or master.
Don't create a PR. Tell the user which plan tasks are unfinished or which checks still fail, what you tried, and what you need from them.
Tell the user the PR is ready: send a push notification (PushNotification tool, if you have it) with the PR title and URL, and end with a short summary: PR link, issue, what changed, tests run.
A session is waiting on you (a brainstorming question, plan approval or a permission).
